slides.sub: This week's body tips in one place

sections.heading: Neck pain when driving
lines: Headrest level with the back of your head.
Every 2 hours: stop, walk, roll your shoulders.

sections.heading: Floor play with kids
lines: Roll to your side, then hands and knees.
Step a foot forward, push up through your legs.

sections.heading: Ankles that keep rolling
lines: Stand on one leg for 30 sec, each side.
Easier? Eyes closed, or on a cushion.

sections.heading: Warm-ups that actually help
lines: Easy jog 3–5 min, then leg swings and lunges.
Finish with short sprints near game speed.

sections.heading: Talking to your therapist about pressure
lines: Give a number: "That's about an 8 out of 10."
Ask for more, less or another area anytime.

sections.heading: Pilates for men
lines: Single-leg bridge: 3 sec up, 3 sec down.
8 each side, keep your pelvis level.

caption:
Hybi's weekly recap for Dec 14 to 19.

When driving, set your headrest level with the back of your head and take a break every 2 hours. Ankles that keep rolling often respond to simple balance work, starting with 30 seconds on one leg. Before weekend sport, warm up with an easy jog, leg swings and lunges, then a few short sprints. And on the massage table, giving a number out of 10 is an easy way to talk about pressure.

Scroll back through the feed for the full comics. Book online via the link in bio 🐱
